subject: Mathematics
title: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator)
equipment: ruler graduated in centimetres and millimetres, protractor, pair of compasses, pen, HB pencil, eraser, and paper for rough work.
instructions: Type your working and your final answer in the boxes for each part.
You must **show all your working**. Marks are given for correct working even if your final answer is wrong.
Diagrams are **not** accurately drawn, unless otherwise indicated.
information: The total mark for this paper is 80.
The marks for each question are shown in brackets. Use this as a guide to how much time to spend on each question.
Aim for about one minute per mark, and keep 10 minutes at the end to check your answers.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Write 7.2 × 10⁻³ as an ordinary number.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Work out (3 × 10⁵) × (8 × 10⁻²).
Give your answer in standard form.

Work out 2¾ ÷ 1⅚
Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.

Ada, Bola and Chidi share some sweets in the ratio 2 : 3 : 7
Chidi gets 30 more sweets than Ada.
How many sweets do they share altogether?

questions.intro: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 24°.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Work out the number of sides the polygon has.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Work out the sum of the interior angles of the polygon.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Solve 3(2x − 1) < 4x + 9

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
n is an integer such that −3 < n ≤ 2
Write down all the possible values of n.

In a sale, all prices are reduced by 15%.
The sale price of a coat is £68.
Work out the price of the coat before the sale.

questions.intro:
A spinner can land on red, blue, green or yellow.
The table shows the probability of two of the outcomes.
questions.after: The probability that the spinner lands on green is twice the probability that it lands on yellow.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Work out the probability that the spinner lands on yellow.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Kemi spins the spinner 200 times.
Work out an estimate for the number of times it lands on green.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Simplify fully (2a³b)⁴

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Work out the value of 27^(−2/3)

Solve the simultaneous equations
3x + 2y = 5
5x − 4y = 23

The length of a rectangle is 8.4 cm, correct to 1 decimal place.
The width of the rectangle is 3 cm, correct to the nearest centimetre.
Work out the upper bound for the perimeter of the rectangle.

questions.intro:
ABC is a right-angled triangle.
Angle ABC = 90°, angle ACB = 30° and AB = 6 cm.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Work out the length of AC.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Work out the length of BC.
Give your answer as a surd in its simplest form.
Solve 2x² + 7x − 15 = 0

parts.text:

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:

questions.intro:
y is directly proportional to the square of x.
When x = 3, y = 36

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Find a formula for y in terms of x.
Hence find the value of y when x = 5

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Find the positive value of x when y = 196

questions.intro: The table gives information about the times, t minutes, that 69 students took to finish a puzzle.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Work out the frequency density for each class interval.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Work out an estimate for the number of students who took between 12 minutes and 20 minutes.

The point P(3, −4) lies on the circle.
Find an equation of the tangent to the circle at P.
Give your answer in the form ay = bx + c, where a, b and c are integers.
Simplify fully (x² − 9) / (2x² + 5x − 3)

parts.text: Work out fg(2)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Find f⁻¹(x)
Prove algebraically that (2n + 3)² − (2n − 3)² is a multiple of 8 for all positive integer values of n.

questions.intro:
OAB is a triangle.
OA = **a** and OB = **b**
M is the midpoint of AB.
N is the point on OA such that ON : NA = 2 : 1

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find the vector AB in terms of **a** and **b**.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Find the vector NM in terms of **a** and **b**.
Give your answer in its simplest form.
Solve x² − x − 12 > 0

A bag contains 5 red counters and 3 blue counters.
Tunde takes a counter at random from the bag and does not replace it.
He then takes a second counter at random.
Work out the probability that the two counters are different colours.

questions.intro:
Here are the first five terms of a quadratic sequence.
4      9      18      31      48

parts.text: Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term of the sequence.

Cylinder A and cylinder B are mathematically similar.
The surface area of cylinder A is 45 cm².
The surface area of cylinder B is 80 cm².
The volume of cylinder A is 54 cm³.
Work out the volume of cylinder B.
